summary: Reviewed CacheableAPIMethodTrait.php — the single modified file.

The inner try/catch(\Throwable $ignored) {} wrapping logError() is correctly structured. It uses \Throwable (not \Exception) for maximum coverage, mirrors the adjacent delete() defensive block exactly, and the return null guarantee is preserved as the final statement of the outer catch.
The log message is well-formed: includes the error code constant value, the corrupt file path, and the original exception message — sufficient for operator triage without noise.
@phpstan-require-implements CacheableAPIMethodInterface annotation on the trait is a strong correctness constraint that prevents misuse — this is good defensive architecture.
One cosmetic note: the logError() block uses multi-line try/catch while the delete() block uses single-line compact style. Non-blocking.

comments.note: Implementation is minimal and correct. The inner try/catch(\Throwable $ignored) {} pattern applied to logError() is exactly the right approach — it mirrors the already-established delete() defensive pattern in the same block, making the two matching constructs easy to read together. The catch correctly uses \Throwable (not \Exception) to catch PHP errors as well, maximising robustness.

The log message format is good — it includes error code constant value, full file path, and the original error message. This gives operators sufficient context for a corrupt-cache alert without requiring a full stack trace in the log.

Minor cosmetic inconsistency: the logError() try/catch uses multi-line formatting while the delete() try/catch uses the compact single-line style. Both are valid; consistency between the two defensive blocks within the same outer catch would be slightly cleaner. Non-blocking style note.
